source_grid.description: NSIDC Sea Ice Polar Stereographic, Hughes 1980 ellipsoid, 25 km

resampling.method: each cell centre is projected from EPSG:3413 into EPSG:3411 and takes the bilinear mean of the NSIDC ocean cells among its four neighbours, weights renormalised over those cells
resampling.coast: a cell with no NSIDC ocean neighbour that a terrain lookup can read takes the mean of its filled 8-neighbours, one ring per pass, so coastal water NSIDC masks as land or coast carries the nearest observed concentration
resampling.reason: NSIDC's grids are on the Hughes 1980 ellipsoid with their own latitude of true scale; the explorer draws this coarser grid as a texture on the sea surface and clips it to each terrain's ocean, so the grid need not match a terrain grid
resampling.latitude_longitude: taken as the same on the Hughes 1980 ellipsoid and WGS84, as NSIDC's grids assume

domain.order: row-major order of the non-zero cells of domain_mask
domain.definition: cells a texture lookup on any terrain's ocean can read (the four cells around each ocean node and one ring more) that hold ice in at least one month; every other cell is open water throughout

frames.empty_note: months whose NSIDC file holds no data: December 1987 and January 1988 (the SSM/I gap of 3 December 1987 to 12 January 1988) in both hemispheres; the Northern Hemisphere file for July 1984 is empty too
frames.layout: frame-major: concentration[frame * cell_count + cell]; the frames are consecutive months, each placed at mid-month

series.scope: Northern Hemisphere (the whole Arctic, of which the Greenland grid holds a part)
series.note: extent is the area of the hemisphere's ocean cells with at least 15 % ice on at least half of the month's days (the files' QA flag), close to the Sea Ice Index's monthly extent, which averages daily extents; area weights the same cells by their monthly mean concentration; both are summed on NSIDC's grid with each cell's area from the projection's scale factor. The map draws the monthly mean concentration, as NSIDC's monthly images do: the area of its cells at 15 % or more, mean_field_extent, is larger, mostly in the marginal ice zone. The trend is the least-squares slope of a calendar month's extent from 1979, also given as a share of its 1981-2010 average per decade

reference_edge.note: the median ice edge of a calendar month: where the cells that held at least 15 % ice in at least half of the 1981-2010 years give way to those that did not

projection.against: the latitude and longitude of every cell in NSIDC's ancillary file

sea_ice_index.product: NSIDC Sea Ice Index, Version 4 (G02135, doi:10.7265/a98x-0f50), monthly extent CSV files
sea_ice_index.note: the packaged extent counts the cells with at least 15 % ice on at least half of the month's days (the files' QA flag), close to the Sea Ice Index's average of daily extents; what difference remains is mostly the algorithm, the Sea Ice Index taking the NASA Team concentration and the CDR the higher of the NASA Team and Bootstrap concentrations in each cell. The extent of the monthly mean field (mean_field_ keys), every cell whose monthly mean concentration reaches 15 %, departs further

source_files.sensor: SMMR > Scanning Multichannel Microwave Radiometer; SSM/I > Special Sensor Microwave/Imager

fields.name: concentration
fields.note: monthly mean sea-ice concentration, whole percent, frame-major (concentration[frame * cell_count + cell]); 255 throughout a month without data

fields.name: reference_ice_frequency
fields.note: percent of the 1981-2010 years in which the cell held at least 15 % ice, one frame per calendar month (January first), month-major like concentration; the 50 % contour is the median ice edge

flags.0: outside the domain (no ice in any month, or out of reach of the terrain's ocean)
